test_title: RRB Group D Official Paper (Held On: 22 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is true for saturated hydrocarbons?

options.text: They have at least one triple bond between carbon-carbon atoms.
They can have either double and triple bond between carbon-carbon atoms.
They have only a single bond between carbon-carbon atoms.
They have at least one double bond between carbon-carbon atoms.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They have only a single bond between carbon-carbon atoms**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Saturated hydrocarbons** are organic compounds composed entirely of **carbon** and **hydrogen** atoms where all **carbon-carbon atoms** are linked by **single covalent bonds**.
 
• These compounds are commonly known as **Alkanes**. Because every carbon atom is bonded to the maximum possible number of hydrogen atoms, they are considered "saturated." ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Hydrocarbons that contain at least one **triple bond** between carbon atoms are called **Alkynes**. These are classified as **unsaturated hydrocarbons**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Hydrocarbons having at least one **double bond** are known as **Alkenes**. Like alkynes, they are also **unsaturated** because they can undergo addition reactions to accommodate more hydrogen. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
• Compounds that contain either **double or triple bonds** are broadly grouped as **unsaturated hydrocarbons**, distinguishing them clearly from saturated ones. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alkanes (Saturated):**
 
 
• The general formula for open-chain alkanes is **CnH2n+2**, where **n** is the **number of carbon atoms**.
 
• Common **examples** include **Methane (CH4)**, **Ethane (C2H6)**, **Propane (C3H8)**, and **Butane (C4H10)**.
 
• They are also called **paraffins** (Latin: parum affinis = little affinity) because they are relatively **unreactive** under normal conditions.
 
 
 
• **Unsaturated Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• **Alkenes**: Contain at least one **C=C double bond**. Their general formula is **CnH2n**. An example is **Ethene (C2H4)**.
 
• **Alkynes**: Contain at least one **carbon-carbon triple bond**. Their general formula is **CnH2n-2**. An example is **Ethyne (C2H2)**, also known as acetylene.
 
• These compounds are more **chemically reactive** than saturated hydrocarbons due to the presence of **pi bonds**.
 
 
 
• **Cyclic Hydrocarbons:**
 
 
• Hydrocarbons can also form **ring structures**. **Cycloalkanes** are saturated cyclic hydrocarbons (e.g., **Cyclohexane**), while **Aromatic** hydrocarbons like **Benzene (C6H6)** possess unique stability and unsaturated ring systems.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Hybridization**: In saturated hydrocarbons (alkanes), each carbon atom undergoes **sp3 hybridization**, resulting in a **tetrahedral geometry** with a bond angle of approximately **109.5 degrees**.
 
• **Physical State**: At room temperature, the first four alkanes (C1 to C4) are **gases**, C5 to C17 are **liquids**, and those with 18 or more carbon atoms are **solids**.
 
• **Combustion**: Saturated hydrocarbons typically undergo **complete combustion** in the presence of sufficient oxygen, producing a **non-sooty blue flame**, **carbon dioxide**, and **water**.
 
• **Applications**: They are primarily used as **fuels** (Natural gas, Petrol, Diesel) and **lubricants** due to their chemical stability and energy content.
